title: Write landing records in land --pr with push recovery
summary: For maintainers running athena land --pr: write a LandingIntent to athena/records and push it before the host merges, then a Landing record (second parent = PR head) after. Unlike the failed attempt, a rejected push or a leftover unpushed local records commit must recover on its own instead of failing with a divergence error.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for each failure path; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria run tests that exercise the behavior.
Fixes the divergence recovery rather than working around it.
Design doc records the recovery choice and failure table.
One focused change on land --pr and the records writer.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The new request is retried job 20261024-114123-p0n4 with the proposed next request as its starting point.

Chosen recovery: push the built commit to the remote with a lease before moving the local ref, or on rejection reset to the fetched tip and re-apply the same record files, then retry a bounded number of times.
Merged-but-unverified: the landing record is written because the host did merge.
docs/design/records-history.md is updated since the design doc must record the recovery decision and failure table.

acceptance_criteria.text: A fake-host test of a successful land_pr reads the records branch and finds a landing-intent record, then a landing record. The intent has PR number, head sha, head tree, expected base and job ids. The landing has PR number, head sha, host commit, merge method, commits with tree/job/verification, and the intent id. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
A test shows the records commit carrying the landing record has the PR head sha as its second parent. Run: cargo test.
A test with a fake host that refuses the merge shows the records branch holds the intent and no landing record, and land_pr returns its existing error. Run: cargo test.
A test recording call order shows the intent is committed and pushed to a bare remote before PrHost::merge is called; the landing record is also pushed.
Test (a): the records push is rejected because the remote moved; the retry (bounded attempts) succeeds and local and remote records tips match afterwards. The test fails without the recovery code.

Test (b): a leftover unpushed local intent, then a remote write to athena/records, then the next land_pr still succeeds without a divergence error, and the merge never happens without its intent on the remote.

Test (c): the merged-but-not-verified state is handled by a stated rule (landing written, since the host merged, or a PrReport warning), and a rerun in that state is tested and does not duplicate records.

Test (d): the drain.rs path of Athena::land_pr writes the same records, or an existing drain test is shown to pass with the real ledger. A commit without a trailer between the base and the head gives an error naming its sha.
Existing land and land_pr tests pass unchanged; cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are clean.

Records use the athena-data history.rs types and are written through the athena-git RecordsWriter, validated before writing. The design doc states whether sync_from changed or a distinct recover path was added, and has a failure-path table (starting state, function called, its behavior in that state).
New functions have doc comments citing the records-history.md section they implement; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

out_of_scope: Other jobs of the records-history plan
Changing how trailers, records under records/ or the work-branch rebuild behave
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: Larger scope than usual: recovery logic, drain caller, several failure-path tests; the previous attempt failed in planning.
